text.p: Gold miner United Paragon said on Wednesday its gold output in 1996 rose to 42,687 tonnes, up 35 percent from 1995.
In its disclosure to the Philippine Stock Exchange, the company did not give the exact production figure for 1995.
The company said its gold output this year was expected to reach 52,500 ounces.
"The record performance was attained inspite of the devastating effects of a typhoon in late 1995," the firm said in a statement.
United Paragon also reported a 24 percent increase to 2,496,546 tonnes in the ore reserve of its Longos mine in central Philippines as of end 1996.

It said the Longos ore reserve is expected to yield an average of 11.54 grams of gold per tonne, resulting in a 28 percent increase in gold content to 925,499 ounces compared to 724,928 ounces the previous year.

"The increase in the gold reserves and the identification of other vein systems which are expected to contribute additional mineable reserves led to the ongoing feasibility study by the company to double the production capacity to 1,000 tonnes per day," it said.
The firm also said it expected an ore reserve of two million tonnes in its San Antonio and Baluarte vein systems, which are adjacent to the Longos mine,
United Paragon said it has blocked 268.425 tonnes of ore, with an average of 13.62 grams of gold per tonne, at the San Antonio and Baluarte vein systems as of end 1996.

At least four foreign firms have expressed interest in joint ventures with United Paragon for the exploration and future development of the San Antonio and Baluarte gold vein systems, the company said.
